parsed.title: Fold ownership contradicts SKILL.md
parsed.detail: PHASE_APPEND.md guardrail says "The fold belongs to `execute-phase`'s fold cycle", but the parent contract skills/replan-findings/SKILL.md guardrails state "`review-change` owns the classification; `fold-findings` owns `folded`." Two different owners (`execute-phase` vs `fold-findings`) are named for the same fold duty inside the same unit's material.

parsed.title: Hand-off route bypasses the router gate
parsed.detail: The hand-off template ends with "a finding owned by product → /design-feature <unit>, then /review-spec, then replan", implying a direct replan entry. SKILL.md's "Load condition (the router decides — never inferred)" section says only the line `node scripts/unit-route.mjs <unit> → route: replan` licenses this contract and "No replan line → this contract is not loaded". The template's "then replan" instructs re-entry without naming the router, contradicting the declared single-entry gate.

parsed.title: "Findings closed by the append" overstates the write
parsed.detail: The hand-off prints "Findings closed by the append: <F1> + <F2> + …", but both files state the append never closes or folds findings: SKILL.md "Never fold the finding in code on this route" and PHASE_APPEND "Never fold here. The fold belongs to `execute-phase`'s fold cycle". The append only adds repair phases; the findings are not closed at hand-off time, so the printed line misreports state to the user and to any downstream parser of the hand-off.

parsed.title: Phase-lint fingerprint format unverifiable against named contract
parsed.detail: Step 3 requires recording `Phase-lint: PASS (8/8) · fingerprint P<n>:<layer>:<n-tasks>:<slug>` "exactly as the planners do", but the referenced phase-contract skill is not included in this slice and the fingerprint grammar (e.g. whether <n-tasks> is the ≤8 task count or a hash component) cannot be validated here; if it diverges from the planners' format the SPEC ledger would carry inconsistent receipts. Flagged as a repair the unit must confirm.
